questions.question: What is the interim behaviour while OQ-01 is open? AC-04.1.1 says to ask for the new canton on every move within Switzerland. The 'New canton of residence' table ('When do we ask?') and information.md say it is asked only for a move to a different canton and never for a move within the same canton. Which one do we build and test against?

Within Switzerland the new canton is 'optional' when the canton stays the same and 'required' when it changes, but we only know whether it changed once the employee has given it. If the employee leaves it blank, do we treat the move as 'no change of canton' and pass nothing to the tax office, or must every move within Switzerland include a canton? As written, a canton change can be missed without anyone noticing.

How do we handle an employee who currently lives abroad and moves to Switzerland? They have no previous canton. Is this a change of canton (the new canton goes to the tax office), is the new canton asked, and is there anything to do for payroll or source tax?

US-04.2 says the previous canton is taken from HR's records 'where possible'. What happens when the records have no canton for the employee, or the recorded canton is wrong? Can the employee see and correct the recorded canton, or do we always trust the records?

What exactly does HR receive on a change of canton (AC-04.1.3)? Only the new canton, or also the previous canton, the valid-from date and the new address? How is HR told that this report needs a tax-office follow-up, as opposed to an ordinary address change?

If an employee moving within the same canton fills in the optional new canton anyway, is that value thrown away (AC-04.1.3 says nothing about the canton is passed on) or kept, for example to update HR's record of the current canton? The trace check notes that the 'nothing is passed on' rule is not backed by any source.

Must the new canton match the postcode and town of the new address? What happens if they don't match, for example canton Bern with a Zurich postcode: block the report, warn the employee, or flag it for HR?

When the employee moves abroad, does the tax office of the canton they leave need to be told, or is informing payroll (FEAT-03) enough? The rule says a move abroad is 'not a change of canton', but no source covers the departure from the canton.
'No list of cantons was given.' Which list of cantons may the employee pick from (the 26 Swiss cantons?), and in which language(s) or naming are the cantons shown to the employee and to HR?

Which canton counts as the 'previous canton' when an earlier reported move has not taken effect yet (its valid-from date is in the future)? The canton currently on record, or the canton from the pending move?

US-04.3 (no unnecessary canton questions) is P2, but it limits how the P1 stories US-04.1 and US-04.2 behave. If it is deferred, do we ask for both cantons on every move, and is that acceptable under G-01?

already_flagged: OQ-01: How a change of canton is detected without asking for the new canton on moves within the same canton (ask always / ask for confirmation first / derive from postcode and town)
OQ-02: Whether the previous canton comes from HR's existing records or is asked from the employee

tech_leaks.quote: The expression cannot show the condition 'if not already in the records'.
tech_leaks.why: Refers to an internal rule expression or engine and its limits. That is about how the rules are implemented, not a business requirement.

tech_leaks.quote: So the expression offers the item for every move within Switzerland, and it is required only when it differs from the previous canton.
tech_leaks.why: Describes how the form or rule engine behaves ('expression offers the item'), which is an implementation decision. It also pre-decides the OQ-01 option in technical terms.

tech_leaks.quote: F-TR-015 (hr_meeting): The new canton is a field, needed for the tax office in case of a change of canton.
tech_leaks.why: Calls the new canton a 'field', a UI/data-model term the source quote does not use. The business need is just the information 'new canton'.

tech_leaks.quote: The country is given by its English name, e.g. "Switzerland" or "Germany".
tech_leaks.why: Fixes how the country value is represented. No stakeholder asked for this. It is an engineering choice, and the canton decision in this feature depends on it.
